newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Indian malaise continues, supply looms.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Indian malaise continues, supply looms.

text.p: Sentiment in the Indian global depositary receipt market continued to be weak after Finance Minister P Chidambaram failed to deliver new tax incentives for Indian corporates.
This is starting to look like a market which shows no sign of picking up," said a trader.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR Index fell 1.20 points, or 1.71 percent to 69.29 points, a premium of 11.42 percent over the local market after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share 52.12 points, or 1.52 percent, to 3,382.71.

"We know State Bank of India is coming with $400 million in the next couple of weeks, what we do not know is whether telephone company VSNL is coming with double that amount in the next couple of months," said a trader.
Indian GDRs are down over 18 percent over the past quarter and over six percent from the start of the year.
The Capel Taiwan Index rose 0.95 points, 1.07 percent, to 90.18 points, a premium of 3.57 percent over the local market after the Taiwan Weighted Index up 39.68 points or 0.62 percent at 6,455.44

The Capel Korea Index fell 0.91 points, 1.33 percent, to 67.77 points, a premium of 21.98 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index shed 1.59 points to provisionally close at 801.45.
